linesVerbatim: ## Language-native product quality
**Proposed V2 product-quality requirement.** A native/Rust distribution core does
not require every analyzer to be implemented in Rust. Implementation language is
chosen per role to preserve or improve the target language's semantics,
ecosystem fidelity, and operational quality—not to force all roles through a
lowest-common-denominator abstraction.
For every language/tooling role the product elects to support, DR-118 and
DR-G13 require:
- an explicit capability/parity matrix against a future product-approved,
digest-pinned role corpus, fixtures, measured baseline behavior/performance,
and accepted current path; the prototype commit supplies source navigation,
not that acceptance manifest;
- language-specific semantic, identity, Coverage, graph, and failure goldens;
- behavior and performance baselines on supported platforms/corpora;
- documented known limitations and unsupported tiers;
- typed unavailability or refusal when required semantics are absent; and
- tests proving there is no silent fallback to a weaker syntactic, semantic, or
graph answer.
TypeScript analysis must meet product-approved parity/improvement thresholds
against the future accepted corpus for the selected scope. Rust analysis must
meet its product-approved Rust-native corpus/capability thresholds. No such
digest-pinned quality corpus or accepted measurement manifest exists in this V2
snapshot, so these are OPEN evidence requirements rather than current quality
claims. The exact languages, tools, tiers, and parity thresholds are product
decisions; V2 does not invent a support list or choose analyzer implementation
languages. This requirement is a blueprint-readiness and review gate, not a
binding implementation choice.

platforms.cellRule: A cell may state platform-invariant explicitly (a verifiable claim). Omitting the axis is unlawful (D-007 item 1 / MF-3).

matrixShape.capabilityBoundary: One row per capability the role's component manifest advertises, derived from the host-contract capability declaration (DR-125). DR-125 is OPEN. That closure is an activation gate for matrix authoring (D-007 OBS-D007-T2-02): this artifact does not treat DR-125 as accepted, does not author a matrix, and does not use DR-125 as a live capability vocabulary. If DR-125 closes by scoped disposition, matrix authoring follows that disposition. The five named areas below are an ILLUSTRATIVE FLOOR, not a closed vocabulary.
matrixShape.manifestIsBoundary: The manifest is the boundary source (D-007 SF-6). This artifact does not invent capabilities the host contract does not declare.
matrixShape.dr125ActivationGate: OPEN. Owner: DR-125. Divergence owner: the DR-125 successor, not this artifact. Matrix authoring waits on that closure or its disposition.

required: prototype-baseline measurement at the pinned commit, or an explicit no-prototype-baseline / prototype-baseline-inapplicable statement
known limitations and unsupported tiers (absence is an explicit claim)
threshold cell (RESERVED; product-approved at matrix acceptance; no silent regression against the stated baseline)
performance-baseline runner and environment (OBS-D007-T2-01). Required when the row carries a performance baseline. Absence is an explicit no-runner-recorded claim, not a default.

knownLimitations.rule: Every row carries documented known limitations and unsupported tiers. A row with none states that explicitly. Absence of limitations is a claim, not a default (D-007 item 2).

baselines.behaviorAndPerformance: Every row carries both. Prototype-measured at a62509d6 where applicable, else the explicit absence statement (D-007 item 3).
baselines.analyzeWorkload: Workload-level RSS/latency for analyze joins the same qualification-harness decision D-006 routed them to. Named here so silence exists nowhere. Numbers are not minted here.
baselines.onlyAdmissibleExistingReference: The prototype at a62509d6 is the only admissible EXISTING-behavior reference, with DR-203 caveats (SHA-1 identity, out-of-corpus custody; re-verified at each measurement). A missing or inapplicable baseline is replaced ONLY by a product-approved language-native corpus (D-007 item 5).
baselines.runnerAndEnvironment: A performance baseline measures nothing reproducibly unless its runner/environment is recorded (D-007 OBS-D007-T2-01). This artifact requires that recording as a per-row field. It does not mint runner classes or numbers.

goldenClasses.identityAndCoverageRide: Identity and Coverage golden classes ride DR-006 (finding fingerprint, subjectScopeCommitment, typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot, capabilityManifestId). Matrix prose can NEVER settle a parked recipe. If DR-006 closes by disposition, dependent rows follow that disposition (D-007 item 6 / D-002 symmetry).

thresholds.rule: Parity-or-improvement per row is a PRODUCT approval at matrix acceptance (the DR-115 pattern of product-owned numbers, not the D-006 numbers themselves). No row ships with a silent regression against its stated baseline (D-007 item 7).
thresholds.whyNoNumbersHere: D-007 rejected THRESHOLDS-NOW: no measured denominator exists pre-blueprint, and inventing numbers would repeat the class D-006's reviewer struck (a threshold whose runner/workload is unnamed measures nothing).
thresholds.doesNotSatisfyByStructureAlone: Integrating this structure does not SATISFY DR-118. D-056 listed DR-118 as Class-B-ineligible while per-row thresholds remain design-undecided.

noSilentFallback.rule: A required NEGATIVE test class per capability: the role REFUSES (typed, loud) rather than degrading to a weaker parser, syntactic tier, semantic model, graph, or finding model (D-007 item 8).

corpusDiscipline.rule: Digest-pinned per file, product-approved before any measurement claim, versioned by supersession. EIR measured-or-cited-at-digest applies to every cell (D-007 item 4).
corpusDiscipline.standing: No digest-pinned quality corpus or accepted measurement manifest exists in this V2 snapshot (file 02). This artifact does not author one.
